newsitem.title: USA: Honda's Acura division sees higher sales.
newsitem.headline: Honda's Acura division sees higher sales.

text.p: Richard Thomas, general manager of Honda Motor Co Ltd's Acura division, said U.S. sales rose about 12 percent in 1996 and the automaker hopes for additional sales growth in 1997.

Thomas, speaking to Reuters at the Los Angeles Auto Show, said Acura sold about 111,000 vehicles in the United States last year. Excluding the Acura Integra sports car, Thomas said Acura sales were up about 77 percent in 1996.
Thomas attributed the improvement to strong sales of its new CL series of cars, the first Acuras to be designed, engineered and manufactured in the United States.
Thomas said Acura's sales increase, coming as other luxury carmakers saw sales decline last year, reflects the addition of new vehicles to its line-up.
"In all fairness, we have almost all new cars in the last 18 months and that's helped us a lot," he said.
In less than two years, Acura has doubled its line-up to six vehicles. For 1997, Thomas unveiled a new version of its NSX sports car and a limited edition Integra R model.
Thomas said Acura hopes 1997 sales will also rise, but he did not give a specific forecast.
